title: Consonant Sounds: Voicing, Clusters and Silent Letters

blocks.text: A candidate in Enugu marks 'then' as the same sound as 'thin' because both start with th. Thin is /θ/ — voiceless, as in think. Then is /ð/ — voiced, as in this. The Oral English paper lives on pairs like that. If you only read the letters, you will miss the mark the examiner is selling.

blocks.markdown:
English has **twenty-four consonant sounds**. Two questions matter for every one of them:

1. **Voicing** — do the vocal cords vibrate? Place two fingers on your throat and say *fan* then *van*. /f/ is voiceless; /v/ is voiced. The mouth shape is the same; only the buzzing changes.
2. **Manner** — how is the air stopped or squeezed? Plosives stop it completely (/p b t d k g/). Fricatives squeeze it (/f v θ ð s z ʃ ʒ h/). Affricates stop then squeeze (/tʃ dʒ/). Nasals send it through the nose (/m n ŋ/).

blocks.title: Voiced and voiceless pairs
blocks.text: Many consonants come in pairs that share place and manner and differ only in voicing: /p–b/, /t–d/, /k–g/, /f–v/, /θ–ð/, /s–z/, /ʃ–ʒ/, /tʃ–dʒ/. WAEC loves to underline one member of a pair and offer the other as a distractor.

blocks.caption: Consonants the Oral English paper tests most

items: **Silent b** — debt, doubt, climb, lamb, plumber, womb.
**Silent k** — know, knee, knife, knock, knowledge.
**Silent w** — write, wrong, sword, answer, two.
**Silent l** — walk, talk, could, calf, yolk.
**Silent h** — hour, honest, honour, vehicle (second h).
**Clusters you must not simplify** — street /str/, glimpse /glimps/, asked /ɑːskt/, texts /teksts/. Dropping a consonant from a cluster is a pronunciation error the paper can test by grouping.

blocks.title: Same letters, different consonant
blocks.prompt: Which word has the same th sound as thin: think, then, this, or breathe?

steps.text: Feel the sound of thin. Air squeezes between the tongue and the teeth; the vocal cords do not buzz. That is voiceless /θ/.
then — /ðen/. The cords buzz. That is voiced /ð/.
breathe — /briːð/. The verb ends in voiced /ð/; the noun breath ends in voiceless /θ/. Same family of letters, opposite voicing.
Only think matches thin. The letters th are doing two different jobs in English.

blocks.title: WAEC Oral English tip
blocks.text: When the underlined letters are th, sh, ch, s or n, say the keyword aloud and decide voiced or voiceless before you look at the options. Then test each option the same way. For silent-letter items, say the word as you would in careful RP: if your tongue never arrives at that letter, it is silent, and a word that actually sounds the letter does not match.

points: Consonants are classified by voicing and by manner of articulation.
/θ/ and /ð/ both spell th; only /θ/ is voiceless.
Silent letters (b in debt, k in know) are not pronounced and must not be grouped with sounded ones.
Clusters such as street and glimpse keep every consonant; simplifying them changes the word.
